The vibrational contribution for a single normal mode is given by \( U_{\mathrm{m},\mathrm{vib}} = R \frac{\theta}{e^{\theta/T} - 1} \), where \( \theta = hc\tilde{\nu}/k \). Using \( hc/k = 1.4388\ \mathrm{cm\,K} \), \( \tilde{\nu} = 900\ \mathrm{cm}^{-1} \), and \( T = 298.15\ \mathrm{K} \):

\[
\theta = 1.4388 \times 900 = 1294.9\ \mathrm{K}
\]
\[
\theta/T = 1294.9 / 298.15 \approx 4.343
\]
\[
e^{\theta/T} = e^{4.343} \approx 76.9
\]
\[
\frac{\theta}{e^{\theta/T} - 1} = \frac{1294.9}{75.9} \approx 17.06\ \mathrm{K}
\]
\[
U_{\mathrm{m},\mathrm{vib}} = 8.314\ \mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}} \times 17.06\ \mathrm{K} \approx 141.8\ \mathrm{J/mol} = 0.142\ \mathrm{kJ/mol}
\]

This matches option J.

ANSWER: J
